questions.name: Choking Relief Across Ages
questions.keyword: universal sign clutch throat hands
questions.text: An adult suddenly grabs the front of their neck with both hands and looks panicked after eating. AHA Part 11 names this gesture by what term?

answers.text: The recovery position signal
The universal choking sign
The agonal gasp posture
The CPR readiness gesture

explanations.a: There is no 'recovery position signal'; the recovery position is a posture for someone breathing normally.
explanations.b: AHA Part 11 names the universal choking sign — clutching the neck with both hands — as the indicator that someone is choking.
explanations.c: Agonal gasping is a sign of cardiac arrest, not choking.
explanations.d: There is no AHA-named 'CPR readiness gesture.'

questions.name: Choking Relief Across Ages
questions.keyword: are you choking nod yes cannot talk
questions.text: You suspect a coworker has a severe airway obstruction. Which question and response confirm it, per AHA Part 11?

answers.text: 'Can you walk?' — mobility confirms severity
'Did you eat anything?' — if yes, proceed
'Are you OK?' — only verbal answers count
'Are you choking?' — if they nod yes and cannot talk, severe airway obstruction is confirmed

explanations.a: Mobility does not establish whether the airway is severely obstructed.
explanations.b: Recent eating is not the criterion for severe airway obstruction.
explanations.c: 'Are you OK?' is the responsiveness check, not the FBAO confirmation question.
explanations.d: AHA Part 11 directs the rescuer to ask 'Are you choking?' and confirms severe obstruction if the person nods 'yes' and cannot talk.

questions.name: Choking Relief Across Ages
questions.keyword: infant severe weak absent cough cannot cry vocalize
questions.text: AHA Part 11's Infant FBAO algorithm lists specific signs of severe airway obstruction. Which set matches?

answers.text: Weak or absent cough, inability to cry or vocalize
Normal breathing and full conversation
Loud forceful coughing and crying
Slowly developing fever and chills

explanations.a: AHA Part 11's Infant FBAO algorithm lists weak or absent cough and inability to cry or vocalize as evidence of severe airway obstruction.
explanations.b: Normal breathing and conversation rule out severe FBAO entirely.
explanations.c: Loud coughing indicates a mild obstruction.
explanations.d: Fever and chills are signs of infection, not airway obstruction.

questions.name: Choking Relief Across Ages
questions.keyword: mild encourage cough monitor no intervention
questions.text: An adult is coughing forcefully and can speak in short bursts after eating. This presentation is consistent with mild airway obstruction. What is the appropriate action per AHA Part 11?

answers.text: Encourage the person to keep coughing and monitor for worsening signs
Lay the person down and start chest compressions
Begin abdominal thrusts immediately
Insert a finger into the mouth to feel for an object

explanations.a: Mild airway obstruction is best handled by encouraging forceful coughing while monitoring for signs of severe obstruction.
explanations.b: Compressions are for cardiac arrest or unresponsive choking, not a coughing, talking patient.
explanations.c: Abdominal thrusts are reserved for severe airway obstruction.
explanations.d: Blind finger probing risks pushing a foreign body deeper.

questions.name: Choking Relief Across Ages
questions.keyword: 5 back blows then 5 abdominal thrusts sequence
questions.text: An adult clutches their throat, nods yes to 'Are you choking?', and cannot speak. According to AHA Part 11's Adult FBAO sequence, what is the correct relief sequence?

answers.text: Give 5 forceful back blows between the shoulder blades, then 5 abdominal thrusts if needed
Lay them down and start chest compressions immediately
Give 30 forceful breaths
Wait several minutes to see if the obstruction clears on its own

explanations.a: AHA Part 11 directs the rescuer to deliver 5 forceful back blows; if those do not relieve the choking, perform 5 abdominal thrusts.
explanations.b: Compressions are reserved for an unresponsive choking victim.
explanations.c: Forceful breaths during severe airway obstruction cannot bypass the obstruction.
explanations.d: Waiting wastes the brief window before unconsciousness in severe airway obstruction.

questions.name: Choking Relief Across Ages
questions.keyword: back blow heel of hand between shoulder blades
questions.text: AHA Part 11 describes how to deliver back blows for choking relief in a responsive adult or child. Which technique matches?

answers.text: Use the heel of your hand to forcefully strike between the shoulder blades
Use a closed fist to punch the lower back
Use the fingertips to tap gently on the upper spine
Use the elbow to drive into the kidney area

explanations.a: AHA Part 11 specifies using the heel of the hand to forcefully strike the person's back between their shoulder blades.
explanations.b: Closed-fist punches to the lower back are not part of AHA technique and may injure the kidneys.
explanations.c: Light fingertip taps will not generate the force needed to dislodge an obstruction.
explanations.d: Elbow strikes to the kidneys are not part of any AHA choking technique.

questions.name: Choking Relief Across Ages
questions.keyword: abdominal thrust fist inward upward above navel
questions.text: After 5 back blows fail to relieve choking in an adult, you proceed to abdominal thrusts. Which technique matches AHA Part 11?

answers.text: Stand behind the person, make a fist, grab it with the other hand, and press inward and slightly upward into the abdomen above the navel
Lay the person down and push laterally on the rib cage
Stand in front and push down on the chest
Press both flat palms on the lower back and squeeze rhythmically

explanations.a: AHA Part 11 describes making a fist with one hand, grabbing it with the other, and pressing inward and slightly upward into the abdomen — the classic abdominal thrust from behind.
explanations.b: Lateral rib pressure in the lying position is not the AHA-described technique.
explanations.c: Pressing on the chest from in front would be chest thrusts, not abdominal thrusts.
explanations.d: Back pressure is not the AHA abdominal-thrust technique.

questions.name: Choking Relief Across Ages
questions.keyword: continue alternating until expelled or unresponsive
questions.text: After your first set of 5 back blows and 5 abdominal thrusts in a choking adult, the obstruction is not relieved. What does AHA Part 11 direct you to do?

answers.text: Stop and wait for EMS without further intervention
Continue alternating 5 back blows followed by 5 abdominal thrusts until the object is expelled or the person becomes unresponsive
Switch immediately to chest compressions while the person is still responsive
Insert your finger deep into the throat blindly

explanations.a: Stopping leaves the obstruction unaddressed.
explanations.b: AHA Part 11 directs the rescuer to continue alternating 5 back blows followed by 5 abdominal thrusts until the object is expelled or the person becomes unresponsive.
explanations.c: Chest compressions are reserved for the unresponsive choking victim.
explanations.d: Blind finger sweeps are explicitly cautioned against.

questions.name: Choking Relief Across Ages
questions.keyword: activate EMS responsive choking adult
questions.text: AHA Part 11 advises calling the emergency response system when dealing with a responsive adult who is choking. When should activation occur?

answers.text: Only after the person loses consciousness
As soon as possible while continuing relief attempts
Only after 30 minutes of failed attempts
Only if abdominal thrusts fail more than 10 times

explanations.a: Waiting until unconsciousness delays EMS unnecessarily.
explanations.b: AHA Part 11 directs the rescuer to activate the emergency response system as soon as possible while continuing choking relief attempts.
explanations.c: Thirty-minute delay before activation is inconsistent with AHA guidance.
explanations.d: AHA does not set a number-of-attempts threshold; activation should occur as soon as possible.

questions.name: Choking Relief Across Ages
questions.keyword: late pregnancy chest thrusts instead of abdominal
questions.text: A visibly pregnant woman in her third trimester is choking on food. AHA Part 11 specifies how to modify the standard adult choking sequence. What is the modification?

answers.text: Use 10 abdominal thrusts to overcome resistance
Use only verbal coaching and never touch the person
Use 5 chest thrusts instead of 5 abdominal thrusts
Wait until after delivery to perform any choking relief

explanations.a: Increasing the number of abdominal thrusts does not solve the anatomical concern in late pregnancy.
explanations.b: Verbal coaching alone fails when the obstruction is severe.
explanations.c: AHA Part 11 specifies that for patients in the late stages of pregnancy, 5 chest thrusts should be used instead of 5 abdominal thrusts.
explanations.d: Choking is acutely fatal; intervention cannot wait for delivery.

questions.name: Choking Relief Across Ages
questions.keyword: cannot encircle abdomen obese chest thrusts
questions.text: You attempt abdominal thrusts on a choking adult but cannot reach around the abdomen because of body size. What does AHA Part 11 instruct?

answers.text: Force your arms around tighter regardless of fit
Substitute 5 chest thrusts when the rescuer physically cannot wrap their arms around the abdomen
Skip the maneuver entirely
Apply pressure with the foot to the abdomen

explanations.a: Forcing a poor reach risks losing leverage and can injure both rescuer and patient.
explanations.b: AHA Part 11 says when the rescuer cannot encircle the patient's abdomen, 5 chest thrusts substitute for 5 abdominal thrusts.
explanations.c: Skipping intervention guarantees worsening obstruction.
explanations.d: Foot pressure is not a recognized AHA technique.

questions.name: Choking Relief Across Ages
questions.keyword: wheelchair chest thrusts when cannot encircle
questions.text: AHA Part 11 includes guidance on choking relief in a responsive person in a wheelchair. Which approach matches?

answers.text: Tip the chair backward and apply pressure to the throat
Use only verbal commands and never physical maneuvers
Lift the person fully out of the chair before any maneuver
Use 5 back blows followed by 5 chest thrusts when the rescuer cannot adequately reach the abdomen

explanations.a: Tipping the chair and pressing the throat are not AHA techniques.
explanations.b: Verbal commands alone cannot relieve a severe airway obstruction.
explanations.c: Lifting out of the chair wastes time and may injure the rescuer.
explanations.d: AHA Part 11 covers responsive pregnant, obese, or wheelchair-using patients with the principle that chest thrusts substitute for abdominal thrusts when the rescuer cannot encircle the abdomen.

questions.name: Choking Relief Across Ages
questions.keyword: see medical follow up after abdominal thrusts
questions.text: AHA Part 11 includes a recommendation that applies to anyone who received abdominal thrusts during choking relief. What is it?

answers.text: They should be told they are fine and sent home
They should be admitted only if they lost consciousness
Anyone who received abdominal thrusts should be seen by a health care professional after the event
They should drive themselves to the hospital alone

explanations.a: Even after relief, a medical evaluation is recommended because abdominal thrusts may have caused internal injury.
explanations.b: Loss of consciousness is not the only criterion for follow-up.
explanations.c: AHA Part 11 says anyone who received abdominal thrusts should be seen by a health care professional, because those thrusts may cause injuries not immediately apparent.
explanations.d: Driving alone after a choking event creates safety risks.

questions.name: Choking Relief Across Ages
questions.keyword: no abdominal thrusts infants use chest thrusts
questions.text: AHA Part 11 explicitly prohibits which standard adult choking-relief maneuver from use on infants?

answers.text: Back blows
Abdominal thrusts
Chest thrusts
Visualization for visible foreign body

explanations.a: Back blows are exactly what AHA recommends for infants — they are not prohibited.
explanations.b: AHA Part 11 explicitly states do not use abdominal thrusts on infants because of the risk of internal injury.
explanations.c: Chest thrusts are part of the AHA infant choking sequence — not prohibited.
explanations.d: Looking for a visible foreign body before removing it is part of the technique, not prohibited.

questions.name: Choking Relief Across Ages
questions.keyword: 5 back blows alternate 5 chest thrusts infant
questions.text: A 6-month-old responsive infant is choking. According to AHA Part 11's Infant FBAO sequence, what is the correct alternating relief sequence?

answers.text: 5 abdominal thrusts alternating with 5 abdominal squeezes
30 compressions and 2 breaths
5 back blows alternating with 5 abdominal thrusts
5 back blows alternating with 5 chest thrusts

explanations.a: Abdominal thrusts and squeezes are not used on infants.
explanations.b: 30:2 is the CPR ratio for an unresponsive infant in cardiac arrest, not for a responsive choking infant.
explanations.c: Abdominal thrusts are explicitly prohibited for infants.
explanations.d: AHA Part 11 directs the rescuer to alternate up to 5 back blows with up to 5 chest thrusts in a responsive choking infant.

questions.name: Choking Relief Across Ages
questions.keyword: infant chest thrust heel hand lower half sternum 1 per second
questions.text: AHA Part 11 describes how to deliver chest thrusts to a choking infant. Which technique matches?

answers.text: 5 quick downward chest thrusts with the heel of 1 hand in the middle of the chest on the lower half of the sternum at about 1 per second
5 firm pinches across the upper sternum at 5 per second
5 abdominal squeezes below the rib cage
5 slow back-and-forth shakes by the shoulders

explanations.a: AHA Part 11 specifies 5 quick downward chest thrusts with the heel of 1 hand on the lower half of the sternum, at a rate of about 1 per second.
explanations.b: Pinching the sternum is not an AHA technique.
explanations.c: Abdominal squeezes are explicitly excluded for infants.
explanations.d: Shaking an infant is dangerous and is never an AHA-recommended technique.

questions.name: Choking Relief Across Ages
questions.keyword: repeat until object expelled or unresponsive infant
questions.text: After your first round of 5 back blows and 5 chest thrusts in a choking infant, the object is not dislodged. What does AHA Part 11 direct?

answers.text: Stop and wait for EMS
Repeat the sequence until the object is removed or the infant becomes unresponsive
Switch to abdominal thrusts since back blows and chest thrusts failed
Lay the infant flat and apply pressure to the throat

explanations.a: Stopping leaves the obstruction in place and allows the infant to deteriorate.
explanations.b: AHA Part 11 directs the rescuer to repeat the sequence until the object is removed or the infant becomes unresponsive.
explanations.c: Abdominal thrusts remain prohibited for infants regardless of outcome.
explanations.d: Pressure on the throat does not relieve the obstruction.

questions.name: Choking Relief Across Ages
questions.keyword: activate EMS responsive choking infant
questions.text: When you find a responsive choking infant, AHA Part 11 directs you to take what additional step?

answers.text: Wait until the infant is fully unresponsive before any activation
Take the infant to a private room first
Activate the emergency response system
Place the infant on their back to relax the airway

explanations.a: Waiting until unconsciousness delays EMS unnecessarily.
explanations.b: Moving to a private space wastes time and adds no benefit.
explanations.c: AHA Part 11 directs the rescuer to activate the emergency response system when finding a responsive choking infant.
explanations.d: Placing the infant on their back can allow the obstruction to settle deeper; AHA uses a face-down position for back blows.

questions.name: Choking Relief Across Ages
questions.keyword: face down head lower than chest forearm gravity
questions.text: AHA Part 11 describes how to position a responsive choking infant for back blows. Which positioning matches?

answers.text: Hold the infant upright, sitting on your knee
Hold the infant face-up with the head higher than the chest
Lay the infant on the floor on their side
Hold the infant face down with the head slightly lower than the chest, resting on your forearm

explanations.a: Upright sitting eliminates the gravitational assist and is not the AHA-described back-blow position.
explanations.b: Face-up with head higher would work against the goal of expelling the object.
explanations.c: Side-lying on the floor is not the AHA-described position for back blows.
explanations.d: AHA Part 11 positions the infant face down with the head slightly lower than the chest and resting on the rescuer's forearm so gravity assists in dislodging the object.

questions.name: Choking Relief Across Ages
questions.keyword: avoid soft tissue throat while supporting head
questions.text: While holding a choking infant face down for back blows, AHA Part 11 cautions against pressing on a specific anatomic region. Which region?

answers.text: The bony part of the chin
The shoulder blades
The soft tissue of the infant's throat
The bony part of the skull above the ears

explanations.a: Supporting the bony chin is part of correct head and jaw support — not the area to avoid.
explanations.b: Shoulder blades are the target area for back blows, not an area to avoid.
explanations.c: AHA Part 11 explicitly warns the rescuer to avoid compressing the soft tissue of the infant's throat while supporting the head and jaw.
explanations.d: The skull is supported as needed during turning maneuvers; it is not the cautioned area.

questions.name: Choking Relief Across Ages
questions.keyword: turn face up head lower thigh chest thrusts
questions.text: After delivering 5 back blows to a choking infant, you turn the infant over for chest thrusts. AHA Part 11 specifies how the infant should be positioned. Which description matches?

answers.text: Stand the infant up against a wall
Place the infant on the floor and step back
Hold the infant face down with the head higher than the trunk
Hold the infant face up with the forearm resting on your thigh, keeping the infant's head lower than the trunk

explanations.a: Standing the infant against a wall is not part of any AHA technique.
explanations.b: Walking away does nothing to relieve the obstruction.
explanations.c: Face-down with head higher is the back-blow position, not the chest-thrust position.
explanations.d: AHA Part 11 instructs the rescuer to hold the infant face up with the forearm resting on the thigh, keeping the infant's head lower than the trunk for chest thrusts.

questions.name: Choking Relief Across Ages
questions.keyword: encircle chest support back transfer between positions
questions.text: AHA Part 11 describes transferring the infant between back-blow and chest-thrust positions. What key technique is used throughout both positions?

answers.text: The infant's head is not supported at any point
The infant is transferred to another rescuer for each set of back blows
The infant is placed down on a surface between each set
The infant's head and neck are supported throughout the transfer, with the rescuer encircling the chest

explanations.a: Head and neck support is essential to protect the infant's airway and spine during transfers.
explanations.b: A single rescuer can perform both positions without requiring a second rescuer.
explanations.c: Placing the infant down between each set introduces delay.
explanations.d: AHA Part 11 describes the rescuer supporting the infant's head and neck throughout the transfer between the two positions.

questions.name: Choking Relief Across Ages
questions.keyword: collapses lower to ground start CPR compressions
questions.text: A choking adult collapses and becomes unresponsive while you are performing back blows. According to AHA Part 11, what is the correct next action?

answers.text: Continue back blows on the unresponsive person on the floor
Tilt the head back further and try abdominal thrusts in the lying position
Lower the person to the ground and start CPR with chest compressions
Wait for the person to wake up before any further care

explanations.a: Back blows on the floor on an unresponsive person are not how AHA directs the transition.
explanations.b: Repeated abdominal thrusts in a lying position are not the AHA-directed transition.
explanations.c: AHA Part 11 directs the rescuer to lower the choking person who has become unresponsive to the ground and begin CPR with chest compressions.
explanations.d: Waiting for the person to wake up does not happen in cardiac arrest.

questions.name: Choking Relief Across Ages
questions.keyword: look in mouth remove visible no blind sweep
questions.text: During CPR on an unresponsive choking adult, AHA Part 11 specifies what the rescuer should do each time the airway is opened for a breath. Which action matches?

answers.text: Skip breaths entirely and only do compressions
Look in the mouth for a visible foreign object and remove it if seen — but do not perform a blind finger sweep
Insert a finger deep into the throat without looking
Press hard on the abdomen during each breath attempt

explanations.a: Compression-only CPR is not the AHA approach during a known FBAO arrest; visualization and removal of a seen object are part of the sequence.
explanations.b: AHA Part 11 directs the rescuer to look in the mouth each time the airway is opened, remove a visible foreign body, but never perform a blind finger sweep.
explanations.c: Blind finger sweeps may push the object farther into the airway and are explicitly cautioned against.
explanations.d: Abdominal pressure during breaths is not part of the AHA unresponsive-choking sequence.

questions.name: Choking Relief Across Ages
questions.keyword: no blind finger sweep push deeper
questions.text: AHA Part 11 warns against a specific finger maneuver in unresponsive choking. Which maneuver does it caution against?

answers.text: A blind finger sweep because it may push the foreign body deeper into the airway
Pinching the lips shut between breaths
Wiping the lips with a clean cloth
Counting compressions on the rescuer's fingers

explanations.a: AHA Part 11 says do not perform a blind finger sweep because it may push the foreign body back into the airway and lodge it deeper.
explanations.b: Closing the lips during a breath is part of mouth-to-mouth technique and is not cautioned against.
explanations.c: Wiping the lips is a hygiene action and is not cautioned against.
explanations.d: Counting compressions on fingers is unrelated to airway management.

questions.name: Choking Relief Across Ages
questions.keyword: after relief proceed check breathing pulse restart care
questions.text: You successfully relieve a foreign body airway obstruction in an unresponsive adult during CPR. According to AHA Part 11, what should you do next?

answers.text: Stop all care because the person is fine now
Administer naloxone routinely after every choking relief
Place the person back in the choking position to verify
Recheck responsiveness, breathing, and pulse; confirm EMS is activated; and provide CPR or breaths as needed

explanations.a: Stopping care prematurely abandons a person who may still need CPR or breaths.
explanations.b: Naloxone is for opioid emergencies; routine administration after choking relief is not AHA guidance.
explanations.c: There is no 'choking verification position'; the rescuer continues normal post-arrest assessment.
explanations.d: AHA Part 11 says after relieving choking in an unresponsive person, proceed as with any unresponsive person — recheck responsiveness, breathing and pulse, confirm EMS, and provide care as needed.

questions.name: Choking Relief Across Ages
questions.keyword: mild obstruction coughing talking able to speak
questions.text: AHA Part 11 distinguishes mild from severe airway obstruction. Which finding indicates a mild obstruction?

answers.text: Complete silence and blue lips
The person cannot cough or speak at all
The person can forcefully cough and speaks in short sentences
Unresponsiveness and absence of breathing

explanations.a: Complete silence and cyanosis indicate severe obstruction, not mild.
explanations.b: Inability to cough or speak indicates severe airway obstruction.
explanations.c: AHA Part 11 describes a person who can forcefully cough and speaks, even in short sentences, as having a mild obstruction; the rescuer encourages continued coughing.
explanations.d: Unresponsiveness with absent breathing indicates cardiac arrest.

questions.name: Choking Relief Across Ages
questions.keyword: severe cannot cough speak or breathe adequately
questions.text: AHA Part 11 lists features of severe airway obstruction in an adult. Which set matches?

answers.text: Loud forceful cough and full-sentence speech
Inability to cough, speak, or breathe adequately
Mild neck soreness after swallowing
Normal breathing with increased heart rate only

explanations.a: Loud forceful cough and full-sentence speech indicate mild, not severe, obstruction.
explanations.b: AHA Part 11 lists inability to cough, speak, or breathe adequately as signs of severe airway obstruction requiring immediate intervention.
explanations.c: Mild neck soreness is not on the AHA severe-obstruction criteria.
explanations.d: Normal breathing with increased heart rate does not meet the criteria for severe obstruction.

questions.name: Choking Relief Across Ages
questions.keyword: medical evaluation after choking event always
questions.text: AHA Part 11 recommends that anyone experiencing signs of choking be seen by a health care professional after the event. Which reason does the manual highlight?

answers.text: They may need antibiotics for infection
Their AED battery may need replacing
There may be complications from the obstruction or from the relief maneuvers that are not immediately apparent
They must receive legal clearance before returning to work

explanations.a: Antibiotics are not the AHA-cited reason for medical follow-up after choking.
explanations.b: AED maintenance is unrelated to choking follow-up.
explanations.c: AHA Part 11 says anyone experiencing signs of airway obstruction should be seen by a health care professional, particularly after abdominal thrusts, because of potential internal injuries not immediately apparent.
explanations.d: Legal clearance is not the AHA-cited reason.

questions.name: Choking Relief Across Ages
questions.keyword: after relief responsive person monitor call help
questions.text: A responsive adult's severe airway obstruction was relieved with one set of back blows. According to AHA Part 11, what is the next action?

answers.text: Immediately leave the person alone since the crisis is resolved
Administer abdominal thrusts preventively even though the object is expelled
Monitor the person, encourage them to seek medical evaluation, and ensure EMS was activated if needed
Begin CPR to confirm the airway is clear

explanations.a: The person still needs monitoring and medical evaluation after an episode of severe airway obstruction.
explanations.b: Preventive abdominal thrusts after object expulsion are not part of AHA guidance.
explanations.c: AHA Part 11 directs the rescuer to monitor the person, encourage medical evaluation, and ensure appropriate help has been summoned.
explanations.d: CPR is for cardiac arrest; the person is responsive, so CPR is not indicated.
